purpose: Address 15 code quality audit findings: remove Phase 2 comments, replace console.log/error/warn with winston logging, add future-date validation on event creation via CreateEventSchema split, add whyVolunteer field with backward-compatible whyVoluntary deprecation, fix unsafe Prisma `as never` cast, consolidate barrel→direct imports, and denormalize totalHours onto User for leaderboard query performance.
riskRationale: The totalHours denormalization is correctly dual-written across all three attendance paths (markAttendance, approveAttendance, checkOut) and the migration backfills existing data. However, read paths in admin.service, levels.service, stats.service (3 locations), users.service, badge-engine.service, and notification.worker still query VolunteerProfile.totalHours instead of User.totalHours, partially defeating the performance goal. Seed data also omits User.totalHours (defaults to 0). The badge-engine test was not updated to mock user.totalHours — will fail. The whyVoluntary→whyVolunteer migration is clean and backward-compatible. No security concern.
breakingChanges: User.totalHours field added to Prisma schema — requires database migration (included)
Leaderboard now queries User.totalHours instead of joining VolunteerProfile — backfilled via migration
whyVoluntary field deprecated in favor of whyVolunteer — API consumers should migrate

text: Well-structured PR that resolves the 15 audit findings with targeted, correct changes. The logger/env circular dependency fix, CreateEventSchema/EventSchema split with future-date validation, and whyVoluntary→whyVolunteer deprecation are all well-executed. The totalHours denormalization is correctly written in all three attendance paths with a proper backfill migration. However, two issues block merge: the badge-engine test was not updated to reflect the new user.totalHours data source (will fail), and several read paths still query VolunteerProfile.totalHours instead of User.totalHours. Both are straightforward to fix.

reasoning: Two unresolved issues block merge: (1) the MOBILIZER badge-engine test mocks profile.totalHours but the code now reads user.totalHours — test will fail; (2) multiple read paths still query VolunteerProfile.totalHours instead of User.totalHours, partially defeating the denormalization's performance goal and creating drift risk. Both are trivial to fix but must be resolved before merge.

message: MOBILIZER badge test mocks prisma.volunteerProfile.findUnique with { totalHours: 25 } but does NOT mock prisma.user.findUnique. Code now reads from user.totalHours via getBatchData, so `data.user` is undefined → 0 hours → MOBILIZER threshold (20) not met → test expects badge awarded but will fail.
suggestion: Mock prisma.user.findUnique to return an object with totalHours: 25. Also update other hour-based tests (INDUCTION, LEADER) that mock profile.totalHours but not user.findUnique.
suggestionCode: vi.mocked(prisma.user.findUnique).mockResolvedValue({ totalHours: 25, createdAt: new Date(), currentLevel: { tier: 1 } } as never);

message: Admin user list reads totalHours from VolunteerProfile (profile.totalHours) via a JOIN instead of User.totalHours. After this PR, admin reports and leaderboard could show different hour totals for the same user if any write path misses the dual-update. Also misses the performance benefit of the denormalization.
suggestion: Switch the Prisma select to read User.totalHours directly from the root User model instead of from the profile sub-query.
suggestionCode:
totalHours: true,
profile: { select: { avatar: true, bio: true } }

message: Level progress reads totalHours from VolunteerProfile via user.profile?.totalHours (requires a JOIN) instead of reading User.totalHours directly on the User model.
suggestion: Update the Prisma select to include totalHours from User root level and remove the profile.totalHours dependency.
suggestionCode:
profile: { select: { currentStreak: true, longestStreak: true } },
totalHours: true,

message: getVolunteerStats reads totalHours via a separate prisma.volunteerProfile.findUnique query instead of reading User.totalHours directly. This requires an extra query/JOIN that the denormalization was meant to eliminate.
suggestion: Replace the separate VolunteerProfile query with a direct User.totalHours read in getVolunteerStats.

message: getAdminStats aggregates prisma.volunteerProfile.aggregate({ _sum: { totalHours: true } }) instead of aggregating User.totalHours directly.
suggestion: Replace with prisma.user.aggregate({ _sum: { totalHours: true } }) — same result, no JOIN, consistent with the single source of truth.

message: getVolunteerImpactData reads totalHours from prisma.volunteerProfile.findUnique instead of User.totalHours, requiring an extra query/JOIN.
suggestion: Replace with prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: volunteerId }, select: { totalHours: true } }).
suggestionCode: prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: volunteerId }, select: { totalHours: true } })

message: User profile endpoint returns totalHours from VolunteerProfile via u.profile?.totalHours (JON) instead of reading User.totalHours directly. After this PR, the profile endpoint and leaderboard could show different hour totals for the same user.
suggestion: Read totalHours from User root level instead of from profile sub-query.

message: Seed data creates VolunteerProfile records with totalHours (12, 8, 20, 5) but does not set User.totalHours for any user. After running `prisma db seed`, the leaderboard will show 0 hours for all seeded volunteers despite their VolunteerProfile having hours.
suggestion: Add totalHours to each User create/upsert in the seed file, matching the corresponding VolunteerProfile values.

message: INDUCTION badge test mocks profile.totalHours: 5 but not user.findUnique. Test passes (0 < 10 threshold) but tests the wrong data source — it should validate user.totalHours.
suggestion: Add user.findUnique mock with totalHours: 5 for correctness, so the test validates the actual code path used at runtime.
suggestionCode: vi.mocked(prisma.user.findUnique).mockResolvedValue({ totalHours: 5, createdAt: new Date(), currentLevel: { tier: 1 } } as never);

message: LEADER badge test mocks profile.totalHours: 60 but not user.findUnique. Test passes (0 < 50 threshold) for the wrong reason — it should validate hours are met while mentees are not.
suggestion: Add user.findUnique mock with totalHours: 60 for correctness.
suggestionCode:
vi.mocked(prisma.user.findUnique).mockResolvedValue({ totalHours: 60, createdAt: new Date(), currentLevel: { tier: 1 } } as never);
vi.mocked(prisma.mentorship.count).mockResolvedValue(1);

message: Leaderboard sortBy: 'hours' always uses User.totalHours (all-time) regardless of the timeframe parameter. When timeframe: 'weekly' or 'monthly', eventsAttended is filtered but hours are still all-time total, creating a semantic inconsistency — users sorted by hours they didn't necessarily earn in the selected period. Pre-existing behavior (VolunteerProfile.totalHours was also all-time) but the denormalization should document or address this.
suggestion: Either (a) document that hours sort is always all-time regardless of timeframe, or (b) compute time-windowed hours via aggregation (accepting the JOIN cost for filtered views), or (c) add denormalized weeklyHours/monthlyHours counters if timeframe-scoped sorting is needed.

message: Notification worker aggregates totalHours from VolunteerProfile (prisma.volunteerProfile.aggregate). After denormalization, this should aggregate from User.totalHours for consistency with the single source of truth.
suggestion: Replace with prisma.user.aggregate({ _sum: { totalHours: true } }).

message: No test coverage for the new whyVolunteer field. The existing test only sends whyVoluntary (the deprecated field). Three scenarios are untested: (a) sending only whyVolunteer, (b) both provided where whyVolunteer takes precedence, (c) neither provided.
suggestion: Add test cases for the three backward-compatibility scenarios: whyVolunteer-only, both-prefer-whyVolunteer, and neither.

message: The @deprecated JSDoc on whyVoluntary reveals internal implementation history. It should be a concise deprecation notice.
suggestion: Simplify to: /** @deprecated Use whyVolunteer instead */
suggestionCode:
/** @deprecated Use whyVolunteer instead */
  whyVoluntary: z.string().max(500, 'Must be 500 characters or less').optional(),

message: The @deprecated JSDoc on whyVoluntary is invisible to HTTP API consumers. Clients sending the deprecated field receive no runtime warning that they should migrate to whyVolunteer.
suggestion: Log a structured deprecation warning in the auth controller when whyVoluntary is provided but whyVolunteer is absent.

message: getBatchData selects totalHours from prisma.volunteerProfile and from prisma.user but only user.totalHours is consumed in the badge criteria. The profile.totalHours fetch is dead data transferred on every badge evaluation.
suggestion: Remove totalHours from the profile Prisma select since it is never read.

message: EventSeriesSchema uses string comparison for time ordering (data.endTime > data.startTime) while the refactored schemas use minute-based numeric parsing via addEventRefinements. Both are functionally correct for HH:MM format but inconsistent. Pre-existing, not introduced by this PR.
suggestion: Apply the same minutes-based comparison from addEventRefinements to EventSeriesSchema for consistency.

message: The 5-second buffer (Date.now() - 5000) in CreateEventSchema's future-date refinement has no inline documentation explaining the clock-skew/form-submission-delay rationale.
suggestion: Add an inline comment explaining the 5-second grace period protects against clock drift and rapid form submission delays.

message: EventSchema (used for PUT /events/:id) lacks future-date validation intentionally, but there is no comment explaining why updates skip this check.
suggestion: Add an inline comment: // No future-date requirement for updates — admins may backdate events.

message: Dual totalHours fields (User.totalHours and VolunteerProfile.totalHours) with no sync mechanism beyond the three attendance write paths. Any future code path that updates one without the other will cause divergence — there is no guardrail.
suggestion: Add a Prisma $use middleware that syncs User.totalHours whenever VolunteerProfile.totalHours changes, providing a safety net against drift.

message: Inconsistent import style: some modules use direct relative imports while others use the @/shared barrel import. The PR aimed to consolidate imports but left some files using the barrel pattern.
suggestion: Standardize on a single import style across the codebase in a follow-up PR.

message: Cleanly resolved the circular dependency between logger.ts and env.ts by switching to process.env.NODE_ENV at module scope — the correct architectural choice for a foundational utility module.
Replaced unsafe `as never` cast with `Parameters<typeof prisma.$on>[0]` — a meaningful type-safety improvement using built-in TypeScript utility types for Prisma event parameter inference.

Clean separation of CreateEventSchema (with future-date validation and 5-second clock-skew tolerance) from EventSchema (without, for updates). The addEventRefinements helper avoids duplication of shared refinement logic.
EndTime comparison in addEventRefinements uses proper numeric parsing (split(':').map(Number) then minute arithmetic) instead of lexicographic string comparison — robust for HH:MM format.

Backward-compatible whyVolunteer/whyVoluntary dual-field handling with nullish coalescing. Both fields are persisted during registration, ensuring old API consumers sending whyVoluntary continue to work without changes.

All three attendance write paths (markAttendance at line 454, approveAttendance at line 591, checkOut at line 795) update both VolunteerProfile.totalHours AND User.totalHours within the same Prisma transaction — prevents drift between the two denormalized fields.

Migration includes both the new columns and compound index, plus backfill SQL to copy existing VolunteerProfile.totalHours → User.totalHours and whyVoluntary → whyVolunteer. The IF NOT EXISTS guards enable safe re-runs.
Replaced console.error/warn with logger.error/warn, giving structured log output with timestamps, severity levels, and proper integration with the application's observability pipeline.
Tests added for CreateEventSchema covering valid future dates, rejected past dates, virtual-event-requires-link, end-before-start, and non-positive capacity edge cases.
